reference: CGHD classifier reached AUC 0.72 on real masks with 0.97 in-domain accuracy; >0.85 here would be a real improvement, ~0.72 means the render domain did not close the gap.
checkpoint_provenance: VERIFIED CONSISTENT by scripts/check_junction_checkpoint.py: best.pt reproduces val_probs.npy to 3.3e-03 and summary.json agrees within float tolerance (worst predicted-positive discrepancy 8 of 8476 = 0.09%). Trained 750 epochs on crossings_v5.npz, best balanced accuracy 0.8241 at epoch 433, in-domain AUC 0.9045. separation_test.conclusion: No separation in EITHER direction, so there is no signal to exploit even by inverting the decision.

verdict: NEGATIVE, and now conclusive. Transfer AUC across every checkpoint tried: CGHD trained on real photographs 0.596; render-trained v3 0.5094; render-trained v5 at 60 epochs 0.5231 (in-domain AUC 0.7469); render-trained v5 at 750 epochs 0.4849 (in-domain AUC 0.9045). The relationship across the three render-trained models is MONOTONE IN THE WRONG DIRECTION: raising in-domain AUC from 0.7469 to 0.9045 lowered transfer from 0.5231 to 0.4849. That is the signature of fitting render-specific artefacts, so more epochs, more capacity or more synthetic data make it worse rather than better -- 12.5x the epochs bought +0.022 in-domain balanced accuracy and -0.038 transfer AUC. The only checkpoint with any real signal is the one trained on real photographs, which is the actionable finding: what is missing is real annotated crossings, not better renders. Self-labeled synthetic renders are closed as an avenue.
